assumptions.closure: Derive one Q_sha bound for the complete heterogeneous byte program, including every production binding-site SHA-256 execution, and instantiate epsilonSha256 at that exact budget before publishing a numerical security level.

assumptions.postcondition: For the separately defined concrete BLS12-377 V- and W-lane fork-target experiments over the deployed setup distribution, reached by fixed structural polynomial-time reducers from the exact S1 fork, the two target-winning probabilities are bounded by epsilonKzgV and epsilonKzgW after including every batch-to-single or fork-selection loss.
assumptions.evidence: S1Bls12377FixedStatementKzg structurally maps the complete S1 fork into concrete V/W false-opening targets, binds one formal statement to exact public parameters through universal Arkworks equations, and proves the wrapper adds zero oracle queries. No semantic Boolean classifier selects a leaf. Polynomial running time and the batch-to-single conversion are not yet proved. This assumption is not currently instantiable for shipping v1: DevSrs is regenerated from a public fixed ChaCha seed, revealing the alpha and beta sampled by TIPA::setup and permitting false openings in both lanes.
assumptions.closure: Replace the reproducible DevSrs with an authenticated BLS12-377 setup whose trapdoors are unknown, bind its ceremony transcript and artifact digest to the shipping SRS registry, instantiate the fixed-statement setup binding from production equations, prove structural polynomial-time certificates and an explicit batch-to-single reduction with its fork loss, then instantiate epsilonKzgV and epsilonKzgW. Changing the SRS necessarily changes the SRS identifier and aggregate proof fixtures; current v1 proof-byte preservation is incompatible with this closure.

assumptions.postcondition: For every fixed BLS12-377 reduction statement and original proof-producing adversary, Bls12377GipaPreForkKnowledgeSecurity selects one local polynomial-time extractor before constructing the fork; under the declared total query bound, the full-FsAccepts accepted root-opening and product-lane game probabilities are bounded by epsilonRoot and epsilonProduct.
assumptions.evidence: The audited extractor interface sees only proof-owned commitments fixed before the randomizer query, materializes its witness in each challenger-visible challenge, derives full verifier acceptance from supported S1 fork executions, and preserves the total oracle-query bound. The theorem consumes the exact two game bounds through Bls12377GipaPreForkKnowledgeSecurity. The exploratory fixed-setup route is not evidence because it uses acceptsFork := True and a circular extractor-compatibility premise. No injectivity of the dimension-reducing commitment map or shipping acceptance conclusion is assumed.
assumptions.closure: Provide a local polynomial-time certificate for every extractorFor output, instantiate both accepted-fork game bounds over a secure globally sampled and authenticated setup, and prove the heterogeneous adaptive statement-selection distribution bridge with any replay or selection loss explicit.
